surfaces.part: top monitor/scale display on the body

answer.evidence: The main body (rows 10-30, 14px wide) starts with a light band in rows 10-15: row 10 is white, row 11 light, row 12 a darker line, and rows 13-15 are very light. Rows 14-15 are the brightest, so the front edge sits at about row 15. Rows 16-17 (L=133) are darker and read as eave shadow. Below that, the front face runs from row 18 to row 30, with a recessed panel or drawer and a small green indicator at rows 21-26. The 8px-wide screen on top (rows 1-9, green light at row 6) stands on the body, so it is decor. The top band is uncertain: rows 10-13 alone could be the top, with 14-15 a highlight on the front face. Even so, the top reads as more than a 2-row rim.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small, roughly 1x2-tile grey-white scale box with a green display on top. It has about 12 visible tones per tile, which is above the hedge (9) and below the cheese stall (17) and roofed well (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline carries a tint and reads as a dark material tone rather than a black sticker line. Shading is somewhat shallower than the references, with about 4 steps on the body against about 6 on the references. The body and plate show some panel breakup and highlight/shadow variation, but little grain. The facts are at or above the simpler references (hedge, bench, lamp), and a careful artist would likely accept it as a small, simple prop beside them. It is slightly lower than the richest references, but not enough to fail.

surfaces.part: upper screen/monitor housing on top of the body
main body top (stepped light top plane with a lighter front band)
front face with recessed display panel and base

answer.evidence: The main body is 14px wide over rows 10-30. Rows 10-11 are a bright, narrower back plane with a lighter edge at row 11. Row 12 is a gray step. Rows 13-15 are a bright full-width band whose bottom edge is at row 15, followed by darker shadow rows 16-17. This reads as a stepped top surface of about 6 rows. Below it is a vertical front face (rows 16-28) with a recessed display panel (rows ~20-26) and a base, then the outline at rows 29-30. The 8px-wide screen above (rows 1-9, green display) sits on the top and counts as decor. The top reading is somewhat ambiguous, because rows 13-15 could instead be a front-facing band.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small scale-station box with a green display and a lighter body. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline leans toward the material colour rather than being a neutral black sticker line. It is simple and a little less textured than the stall and well, but about as rich as the bench, hedge and lamp, which are also small, simple props. A careful artist would accept it beside them without it looking flatter or more sticker-like.

surfaces.part: main cabinet front face with scale tray panel

answer.evidence: The small monitor on rows 1-9 (8 px wide, green screen) sits on top of the cabinet, so it counts as decor. The main body is 14 px wide from row 10 to row 30. Rows 10-15 form a light top band: a bright strip on rows 10-11, a thin darker row at 12, and a light band on rows 13-15 whose brightest rows are 14-15. That band ends in a front-edge line at row 15, followed by darker shadow on rows 16-17 (L about 133). Below it is a grey front face on rows 16-30, with a tray or panel on rows 20-26. The read is borderline: the band could be a flat front strip, but the edge line plus the shadow rows support a top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a narrow, roughly 1x2-tile prop: a grey-white scale body with a small green display and a plate. It shows about 4-5 lightness steps on the body and a tinted dark blue-grey outline. The facts support this: 12 visible tones per full tile (hedge 9, stall 17, well 20), 0% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outline is tinted rather than black. Judged by eye, it is simpler than the stall and well, with less grain and fewer clusters. It is still not a flat sticker, and it is comparable to the hedge and ahead of the thin bench and lamp, which have a similar total colour count. A careful artist would likely accept it next to the references, though it is slightly lighter on texture detail.

surfaces.part: monitor / display housing on top of the body
main body front face (light band, panel and display)

answer.evidence: The main body spans rows 10-30 at a constant width of 14. Its only top-like feature is a 1-2 row light strip at rows 10-11 (L=246 then 213), with a darker row at 12 (L=124). That is a rim or lip, not a real top plane. Below it, rows 13-15 are a light front-facing band, followed by a grey panel with a small display and button at rows 20-26. All of this is a vertical face with no ellipse, roof or visible contents. The small screen at rows 1-9 (width 8, with a green readout) is a monitor on top of the body, so it counts as decor. The body is drawn almost entirely as a front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small grey-white scale box with a green display on top. It carries 12 visible tones per 16x16 tile, which is above prop-hedge (9) and within range of the stall (17) and well (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no 5x5 flat fills. Its dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline leans blue-grey and follows the material instead of being a uniform black sticker line. It reads as about 4 lightness steps on the body and 3-4 on the screen, a little shallower than the 5-6 on Beodeul pieces. Only 14 colours in total, against 38-40 on the stall and well, make it somewhat simpler. For a small, plain single-tile appliance it is still acceptable beside the references.
